Deepline. The city under the city. Ninety years of rust, neon and people the sky threw away.
He's moving! Trash-heap guy is ALIVE!
...Where is this? Who... who am I?
Dunno! You dropped out of a sky-pipe three nights back. Your hair crackles when you sleep. We call you Sparks.
Mags has been feeding you. Go say thanks - her bun stall is just east. Move with A and D.
On your feet at last. Sit. Eat. Pepper bun, straight off the steamer.
(It's hot. It's good. I know this taste... why am I crying?)
That one's on credit, Sparks. Here, take a spare for the road. Press Q when you need it.
Tusk's crew shake my stall down every week. Three of them are waiting past the rooftops. I can't pay.
You don't know who you are. But I watched you get up. Go and see what your hands remember.
Rooftops are east. Jump with K. Drop through a ledge with S + K. Mind the long fall.
Tusk is DOWN? Ha! Buns are free for you, Sparks. For a week. Maybe two.
Throwing darts, buried in the junk. My hand already knows the weight.
(They hum when I hold them. Something in me is... charged.)

SPARK DART - press U to throw (costs 25 Volt).
Hold J + K to charge Volt. Landing hits charges it too.
So this is the stray that crawled out of my trash and broke three of my collectors.
The stall's closed for collections.
Tusk. Put him back in the heap. I have a shaft to run.
With pleasure, boss.
Hold S to GUARD. When he flashes white, get ready - and DASH (L) through his charge.
SPARKS BEAT TUSK! Did you see that?! He did the lightning thing!
(My name is Kael. I'll tell them later. 'Sparks' isn't so bad.)
The old Cartographer in the Neon Market has been asking about you. Go east - follow the storm-eye tags.
PUBLIC NOTICE FROM AURELIA: "Halcyon Ascendancy seeks escaped SUBJECT 31. Dangerous. Reward: full citizenship."
(Subject 31. Someone up there fell out of the sky too.)
So the tags led you here. I painted them - the storm-eye, the old mark of Vharra. Our mark, boy.
Vharra. The grass. The thunderheads. I saw it in the shard.
When the sky tore, it did not only take our home. It shredded what we WERE - memory, power - into Memory Shards.
Find them and you find yourself. The Pit pays in creds and rumours: win three ranked fights and people will talk to you.
And know this: Grist the Rat King holds the only shaft to the surface. You are not ready for the Sump. Yet.
You carry frost on you, girl. Not one of mine - Ilmaren, yes? Another world the sky swallowed.
A white-haired boy came through here. Stubborn as weather. If you meet him - you are hunting the same people.
The shards hum when you are near. Listen for them. The world is wider than these tunnels.
Madame Quill's. Everything here fell off a maglev. No refunds, no questions.
The Pit's through the red door. Anvil's the champ. Nobody's ever knocked him down.
Fresh meat! Three ranked wins gets you the rookie purse. Step in the cage?

Rookie purse is paid, champ-in-waiting. Higher tiers open when the Pit reopens next season.
Spar anyway

THREE FOR THREE! Rookie purse: 500 creds. Don't spend it all on buns.
You fight like someone with something to remember. I know that stubbornness. Don't know from where.
Found this in the cage sand after my first title. It never hummed for me. It's humming now.
THREE FOR THREE! Rookie purse: 500 creds. The crowd likes the cold one.
You move like you're listening to something the rest of us can't hear. Keep listening.
Easy - you're bleeding on my floor. Sit still.
I'm Tamsin. I patch up half of Deepline with whatever I can scrounge.
Grist's gangers dragged my medicine crate into the flooded tunnels. Without it, the clinic closes.
Bring it back and I'll keep you standing for as long as you keep picking fights.
The crate is east, past the dead trains. Watch the green water - it bites.
You got it back. All of it. Hold still, let me look at that arm.
She hums while she works. An old tune. You know the next line before she sings it.
...How do you know that song? That's a Vharran cradle-song. Nobody down here -
I don't know. I just do.
Then we're from the same sky. Call me when it gets bad out there, Sparks. I'll come running.
ASSIST unlocked: TAMSIN. Press O to call her - she heals you. 20 s cooldown.
Clinic's open. Sit down, you look terrible.
You climbed out of my trash. You broke my Tusk. Now you stand in my Sump.
Everything that goes UP pays me. And you have nothing left to pay with but bones.
...The shaft... is yours. It was only ever... a way out.
Something bright is lodged in the wall behind his throne. It has been waiting.
A heavy hatch seals the Metro Shaft. A rat-skull crest is welded over the lock. Grist's.
Aurelia. The city above the clouds. Med-Lab Sector 7, property of the Halcyon Ascendancy.
(Glass. Cold. Alarms. I do not know this place. I do not know ME.)
- can you hear me? Subject 31? Don't answer. Just move. A and D.
There's a wall panel to your right. Get to it and press E. I'll explain when you're not standing in a puddle.
There you are. I'm Wren. I live in the walls - don't think about it too hard.
Halcyon fished you out of a tear in the sky and bottled you like a battery. I want to know why.
Take this med-gel from the dispenser. Press Q to use it.
The floor east of you is flooding with coolant. Climb the shelving: K jumps, S + K drops through a ledge.
Something is in that corridor. My cameras show nothing. But you're staring right at it.
(A white mask. Empty eyes. Nobody else can see them. My hand - it is GLOWING.)

PULSE BURST - press U (costs 25 Resonance). Fists pass straight through a Husk.
Hold J + K to charge Resonance.
Subject 31 is out of its bottle. Disappointing.
Warden-01: contain. I want it intact - the Engine does not run on corpses.
Hold S to GUARD. Watch for the red aiming line: JUMP the low beam, stay down for the high one.
You just scrapped a Warden with your bare hands. I'm updating my threat model.
The admin wing is ahead. Three terminals. Plug me into each (E) and I can open Block C.

FILE: SUBJECT 31. Origin: ILMAREN (extra-dimensional). Resonance output 400% of baseline.
Recommended use: POWER SOURCE.

FILE: CONVERGENCE ENGINE. First full-power test tore two worlds into ours.
SECOND PULSE: charging. Projected result: permanent merge. Donor worlds drained.
FILE: BLOCK C. Captive 'Tidesinger'. Output stable. DO NOT OPEN.
That's three. I'm in. I can scramble their guards for you now - press O when you're cornered.
ASSIST unlocked: WREN. Press O - she stuns every enemy on screen. 20 s cooldown.
Not yet - I need the other two terminals first. One is back near the Warden's hall, one is up on the catwalk.
A notice on the wall: WANTED IN DEEPLINE - agitator known as 'SPARKS'. White hair, red scarf. Assaulted licensed collectors.
(Someone down there is giving them trouble too.)
Block C is sealed. I need all three admin terminals first.
Child of the ice... I do not know your face. But I know your note.
They're draining you.
To feed their Engine. There is little of me left. Better that it sings in your hand than in their machine.
She sings one long, cold note. Coolant climbs out of the cell wall and hardens in your grip.
Go. The docks. In this city the only way out is DOWN.
Do not wait for me. A song does not need its singer to be carried.
End of the line, Subject 31. The Skylift does not run for runaways.
Then I'll find another way down.
You'll find the floor.
...Magistrate. I had it contained -
Enough, Captain. The board does not chase strays across its own docks.
You carry a stolen song, girl. Carry it somewhere lower.
The deck opens beneath you. The Garbage Chute swallows the sky.
Sunlight. Real, dusty, orange sunlight.
(There's a city. In the SKY.)
You hit a mountain of scrap, then sand. The sky you fell from is a shadow far above.
(I fell out of the world. And I lived.)
Easy, stranger. Scrapton's caravans take in anyone who walks out of the Flats alive.
Name's Marlo. That shadow up there is Aurelia. Everything down here is what it threw away. Us included.
Odile will see to your cuts. When you can stand up straight, the bounty board always has work.
West is the Ash Dunes. East, the Glowwild. Neither one is safe, which is why the pay is good.
Hold still. ...There. You're not from here either, are you? It's all right. Hardly anyone is.

BOUNTY BOARD. Jobs for the Ash Dunes and the Glowwild are pinned here.
(Act 2 opens in the next build.)
An old metro shaft, sealed from below. You cut the rat-skull lock off the hatch. Something down there smells of neon and noodles.

The Boy and the Storm
Grass to the horizon. Thunderheads stacked like mountains.
A boy runs ahead of the storm, laughing. The lightning never touches him.
Someone calls a name from the camp, over and over.
...Kael.
My name is Kael.
The Standing Stones
A ring of stones, humming before the rain.
An old woman plants a carved stake in the earth - and the lightning OBEYS her.
"You do not chase the storm, Kael. You give it somewhere to land."
The Night the Sky Tore
The sky over the camp split like wet cloth. Violet light. Screaming.
You stood at the edge and drove your whole body through the storm wall.
It did not stop the tear. But everyone behind you had time to run.
The Frozen Harbour
A harbour locked in ice. Ships asleep in the floes.
A woman at a forge of blue fire sings one long note - and a blade rises out of the sea.
She turns. She is smiling. She says a name.
...Nyra.
My name is Nyra.
The Smith's Note
Every Tidesinger blade is one held note, frozen.
Yours was sung the winter you were born. It was waiting for your hand.
This one is borrowed. It is enough. WINTERLINE.
One Cut
Falling. Wind. The sky shrinking above you.
The blade remembers before you do: one cut, drawn along the ground.
The ice runs ahead of you like a lit fuse.

Lightning Climbs

"Lightning does not fall, Kael. It CLIMBS. Watch it sometime."

A boy lies flat in it beside a wolf made of stormlight. Neither of them breathes.

A horn sounds from the camp. Someone is calling the hunters home by name.
The Clap Before the Rain

The pack-mother strikes her palms together once - and the sky answers through her.

The Wolf That Stayed
The sky over the steppe tore open. Violet light. The herd scattering.
You whistled, and the storm-wolf came, and stood between the tear and the camp.
It did not run when you fell. It is still out there. It has been waiting for the whistle.
Claws on Stone
The storm-wolf went up the cliff face as if it were level ground.
You followed with your hands crackling, each grip a small bite of lightning in the rock.
At the top it looked back at you. That was the day it stopped being a hunt and became a pack.
The Warden of the Stones
Mountains like the knuckles of the world, and below them a ring of standing stones.
A giant of a man walks the ring at dusk, laying one hand on each stone. Each one hums back.
Children follow him, daring each other to touch his shadow.
One of them shouts a name, and he turns, slow as weather, and smiles.
What the Ground Holds
A rockslide above the high pasture. Herders frozen on the path.
You did not run. You knelt, and put both fists to the ground, and ASKED.
The slide parted around them like a river round a stone.
The Dragon Under the Ring
The sky tore over the standing stones. Violet light pulled at the ring itself.
You called down - past the roots, past the bedrock - to the old thing asleep under the mountain.
It rose, and held the stones in place while everyone ran. Then the ground closed over you both.
Hand-holds
You never climbed the mountain. You asked it, and it made room for your hands.
Every hold was there before you reached for it.
"The stone remembers its warden, Brakk. Wherever the sky drops you, put your hand on a wall."
The Ridge Runner
A ridge above the steppe where the wind never stops.
A boy runs along it with his arms out, scarf snapping behind him like a flag.
He jumps a gap between two rocks that no one should be able to jump. The wind holds him a moment too long.
Below, the herders shout his name - half scolding, half laughing.
Lift
The kite-fliers of the ridge did not pull their kites up. They asked the air to rise.
You asked once, as a joke, standing under your little sister.
She went up laughing. It took the whole camp to talk her down.
The Eye of It
The sky tore, and the wind went mad trying to fill the hole.
You ran INTO it. Round and round the tear, faster, until the air ran with you.
A wall of wind stood between the camp and the wound. You were the middle of it.

The wind taught you to let go. The cliffs taught you the other thing.
A gust pinned you to the rock face once, flat as a leaf, and held you there until you found the handholds.
"See?" it seemed to say. "I can do gentle, too."

A storm-season festival on the steppe. Every clan has brought something to throw at the sky.
A girl with burnt eyebrows sets down a tube she built herself and tells everyone to stand further back. Further.
The sky turns gold from one horizon to the other. The thunder itself goes quiet to watch.
Then the whole camp is shouting one name.

Wolves at the herd, every night for a week.
You did not chase them. You buried six clay pots along their trail and went to bed.
In the morning there were six craters, and no more wolves.
The Big One
The sky tore. Everyone ran from it. You ran to your workshop.
Everything you had ever built went into one casing, with the shortest fuse you ever cut.
You aimed it at the hole in the sky. It did not close the hole. But it made the hole FLINCH.

Charged grips, one for each hand, that bit into iron-stone and would not let go until you told them to.

A child tugs her sleeve and says her name like a question.

The harbour ice groaned one winter, and a raiding ship came in over it.

The children of the harbour ran on ice they made themselves, a step at a time.

A frozen harbour at dusk. One by one, lamps come alight along the sea wall.
Nobody sees who lights them. There is only a scarf, red against the snow, already at the next lamp.
The harbour sleeps safe because something it never sees walks the wall all night.
An old watchman raises his cup to the dark and says a name, fondly.
Behind You
A cutpurse on the harbour stair, running, laughing, certain he was clear.

You were not behind him.
The Long Cut
White light. A room with no shadows in it, built that way on purpose.
They forgot the one under the table.
You crossed the room in a single line. Everything on that line had been standing. Then it was not.
Stepping Stones
The harbour children ran on ice they froze under their own feet.
You could never do it their way. You did it yours:
a foot placed on a falling snowflake, a rooftop, a held breath - anything, for exactly as long as it was there.

The Husks are thick near the tower. Fists go straight through them - use whatever it is you people use.
Tower's east, past the pools and the overpass. Stay off the green water. Stay off the green EVERYTHING.
HALCYON RELAY 7-G. STATUS: HARVEST. Rift residue is being drawn out of the soil and beamed up to the Convergence Engine.
LOG: 'Residue yield insufficient. Accelerant introduced to local fauna. One specimen has exceeded containment mass.'
(They're farming the wound they made. And they FED something to do it.)
(The second pulse. They are fuelling it with what is left of our worlds.)
(Bait. They fattened a beast on stolen sky. Now it is loose.)
(They do not even mourn what they break. They only weigh it.)
(That is the breathing under the roots. They woke it.)
(Of course there's a lab at the bottom of this. There's ALWAYS a lab.)
(That is why the air will not move. They have been holding its breath for it.)
(They capped a vent to feed a machine. Twice now. They do not learn.)
(That's a terrible containment spec. I'd be insulted if I weren't about to exploit it.)
(A harvest. And a thing they could not hold. Both ends of this are mistakes.)
You pull the main breaker. The hum dies. Somewhere east, something very large notices it is no longer being fed.
The ground lifts. It is not the ground.
...That's a big one.
So this is what they grow.
At last. Something worth hunting.
Poor thing. They made you hungry and left.
Easy. Easy now. ...No. It will not listen.
Oh, you are going to burn BEAUTIFULLY.
I am going to need a bigger gust.
Come here. I will warm you through.
Finally. A target the right SIZE.
Too large to hide from. Then I will not hide.

When it rears and flashes white, it CHARGES: jump it or dash (L) through, and it dazes itself on the wall.
Stay out of the glowing spit.
The Glowmother folds in on herself. The light under her shell gutters - and something bright rolls free of the wreckage.
A Memory Shard. It was INSIDE her. Halcyon was not only harvesting residue. They were harvesting us.
Three standing stones, half drowned in ash. Under the grey there is a carved eye, with a storm inside it.
(Storm-eye. OUR mark. These didn't fall from the sky. Somebody raised them. Somebody from home was HERE.)
You lay your hand flat on the stone. Every hair on your body stands up. The sky answers.
("You do not chase the storm. You give it somewhere to land." ...I hear you, old woman. I hear you.)
A cairn of bones, stacked the way a pack stacks them: skulls outward. A challenge-marker.
(Something rules these dunes. Not the Baron. Something that hunts the hunters.)
Your howl rolls out across the ash. For a long moment, nothing. Then the dune itself stands up.
(Pale as bone. Twice my height. It has been alpha here for a long time. It looks tired of it.)
The Pale Alpha falls. Out in the dunes, a dozen voices take up your howl. The pack has a new leader.
(A pack. I have a pack again.)
A boulder the size of a house plugs a cave mouth. There are hand-prints worn into it. Very large hand-prints.
(Someone my size moved this. Often. ...I think it was me.)
Roll it
Leave it
The cavern is ringed with standing stones no taller than a child. Practice stones. A warden trained here.
(Each one hums as I pass. They know me. I set them, one a year, for the children who followed me.)
At the centre: a warden's cache, sealed with a slab only one pair of hands could lift.
(I was not only pulled through the sky. I had been HERE before. My world and this one were already touching.)
A wrecked turbine, hung with hundreds of chimes cut from old tin. On a dead-still day, every one of them is ringing.
(Kite-clan chimes. Tuned to the ridge wind. Somebody hung these to call it - and it CAME. It's been waiting here for someone to answer.)
You hold out your scarf. The whole wreck sings one chord, and the wind comes down out of the sky to stand beside you.
(There you are. I thought I had lost you in the fall.)
An Ashfall War bomb, nose-down in the ash, fins still on. Ninety years old. Unexploded. Ticking, very faintly.
(Oh, you beautiful, terrible thing. Barometric trigger, corroded. Secondary still live. Nobody's dared touch you in ninety years.)
Eleven minutes, one spoon, and a great deal of muttering. The ticking stops. The core comes out in your hands, humming.
(I am keeping this. For a special occasion.)
A seam of clear ice runs through the glowing rock, cold enough to burn. Inside it, very faintly, someone is singing.
(A held note. A Tidesinger's note. It has been holding for a long time.)
Sing back
...A voice. A living voice. Child, how long have we been singing?
I do not know. I do not remember the harbour. Only that it was cold, and it was home.
Our ship came through the tear with you. We froze the hull so the glow could not take us. It took everything else.
We cannot leave the note. But you can carry it. Take what the choir has left - and sing it somewhere warm.
Go on, child. A song does not need its singers to be carried.
A dead tree, white with frost in the middle of the green heat. In its highest fork: a nest woven from ice.
(An eyrie. Here. One of them came through with me - and it has kept this one tree cold all this time, waiting.)
You raise your arm. The frost on the branches stirs, and lifts, and becomes wings.
(You waited. Of course you waited. I am sorry it took me so long to remember your name.)
A Halcyon drop-pod, half sunk in the moss. Its beacon sweeps red. On the hatch: RETRIEVAL - SUBJECT 44.
(They sent a machine all the way down here. For ME.)
Kick it
Walk away
"SUBJECT 44 CONFIRMED. THERMAL RETRIEVAL PROTOCOL. PLEASE REMAIN CALM AND NON-COMBUSTIBLE."
You built it fireproof. That's adorable.
Retrieval Unit 03 slumps, its plating run like wax. In its hold: your intake file, and everything they took off you.
("Subject is to be recovered or DENIED TO OTHERS." ...Good. Let them be afraid.)
A volcanic vent, capped with a Halcyon steel plug and gone cold. The moss around it is dead in a perfect circle.
(They put a lid on it. To feed their tower. It has been holding its breath for months.)
You set both palms on the plug. It glows red, then white, then it is not a plug any more. The vent breathes out.
(There. Sleep, or wake - but nobody decides it for you. Not again.)
A Halcyon courier, long dead, sat against a root as if resting. One hand is still closed round a sealed case.
(He hid before he died. Well enough that his own people never found him. I would have chosen this spot too.)
The case opens to the third lock-pattern you try. Inside: creds, a field kit, and a list of every subject taken from the ice.
(Names. Mine is on it. So are forty others. ...Thank you, stranger. I will finish your run.)
Standing stones, cold under the ash. They are waiting for someone else.
A cairn of old bones. Whatever answers here would not answer you.
A boulder the size of a house plugs a cave. Nobody could move that. Almost nobody.
A wreck hung with tin chimes. They are ringing, and there is no wind. Not for you.
An unexploded bomb from the old war. You are not touching that. Someone braver, or madder, might.
A seam of ice in the rock, humming one long note. It is not your song.
A frozen tree in the green heat. Something is nesting in it, waiting for someone.
A Halcyon drop-pod. Its scanner sweeps over you and moves on. It wants someone else.
A cold vent under a steel plug. Whatever could open that is not you.
Something is hidden among the roots here. You cannot quite see where. Someone else would.

Deepline. A shrine built into a dead air shaft, hung floor to roof with paper wishes. Nobody remembers who it was for.
There. Eyes open. I'd started folding you a funeral crane, and I'm not unfolding it now, so mind yourself.
...Paper. Everywhere, paper. My hands want to fold it. I look for my own name and there is only a blank sheet.
You fell down the shaft three nights back in a cloud of the stuff. Not a mark on you. I've been calling you Crease.
I'm Ribbon. I keep the wishes. Come over here - A and D - and press E. Don't tread on anybody's hopes.
Brother Cinder is coming up the shaft. He burns whatever he can't read, and he can't read. He's heard there's a new wish in my shrine: you.
Pepper bun. Eat. Q when you're hurting.
Up the stair, then over the flooded vent: jump with K, and dash in the air with L. The first crane ever folded here is past it. I think it's yours.
Whatever you do, girl, something made of paper does it again behind you. Use that. Throw once, hit twice.
Paper. Paper everywhere, and not one word of it mine. Burn the shrine, boys. Start with the new one.
The oldest crane in the shrine, brown with age. It unfolds in my hands as if it had been waiting.
(Inside, in my own writing: FOLD YOURSELF SMALL AND GO. ...There are two of me standing here. One of us is paper.)
Ten thousand wishes, and every one of them says the same thing: not you, Cinder. Never you.
Nobody wrote that. You only think they did.
Then I'll burn them, and read what they say in the smoke.

Hold S to GUARD his torch. His firebombs leave burning ground - keep moving.
When he flashes white and lunges, DASH (L) through it. Your paper double repeats every skill: throw once, hit twice.
He's gone down the shaft, still smouldering. And not one wish singed. I'll fold him a crane too. He needs one more than most.
(Kiri. It was written on the inside of the first fold, where nobody would look. KIRI. That is my name.)
The shrine stair comes up in the Neon Market. There's an old map-maker there who paints storm-eyes on the walls. Take him a crane.
Deepline. Mile Zero: the buffer stop where the last metro line ends, and the people who walk the tracks make camp.
He's up! Hey - HEY - don't stand yet, you've got no skin on your feet.
...I was walking. I've been walking a long time. I don't know where from. I don't know who that makes me.
You came in off the dead line three days back, still walking, fast asleep. Nine hundred miles of tunnel behind you, the gangers reckon. I've been calling you Miles.
I'm Spike. I walk track. Come here - A and D - and press E. Slow.
Ganger Ballast owns this camp. Anybody who walks in owes him a mile of laid track. You owe him nine hundred.
Pepper bun. Q when you're hurting.
The rail bed's flooded east of here: jump, then dash in the air with L. Your boots are on the far side. Ballast took them. He said nobody walks out of Mile Zero.
You hit harder the longer you keep hitting. I watched you do it in your SLEEP. Don't stop once you've started.
Nine hundred miles of my track, walked without paying. Gang: lay him down.
J: attack - tap for a 4-hit combo. Every hit in a row adds to your MOMENTUM: keep the combo going and each one lands harder.
My boots. The soles are worn through, and I know every mile that did it.
(I lace them up, and my legs remember. Not where I've been. Only how to GO.)
You owe me nine hundred miles, walker. I'll take it out of your legs.
I'm not stopping here.
Everybody stops here. That's what the buffer's FOR.

Hold S to GUARD his sledge. When he LEAPS, get out from under him and jump the shockwave.
When he flashes white he CHARGES: dash (L) through, and he dazes himself on the wall. Then keep your combo going: MOMENTUM does the rest.
You kicked Ballast over his own buffer stop. Nobody's ever gone past the buffer stop.
(Tarn. A small cold lake, high up, where a road ends. Someone named me for the place they stopped walking. I was not meant to stop.)
Track lift goes up to the Neon Market. There's an old map-maker there. Ask him how far it is to wherever you're going.
Aurelia. Med-Lab Sector 5: the Hydro Ward. Forty therapy tanks, and in one of them, a woman they could not keep dry.
(Water. Warm, still, the wrong salt. I reach for the tide and there is no tide. I reach for my name and there is no tide there either.)
- Subject 21? Oh good, you're a floater, not a sinker. I'm Wren. I live in the walls.
They've had you in that tank a month. Every time they drain it, it fills back up. Nobody can work out where you keep the water. Sector 7's breakout just pulled the whole shift off this floor.
The tank release is on the console to your right. A and D, then E.
The tank opens. The water does not spill. It follows you out and waits at your heel.
...Right. Okay. Med-gel on the wall: Q to use it.
Two techs and a guard ahead, mopping. They cut the salt-water line to this ward to weaken you. The valve is past the drained pool. I'd open it.
They've got mops. You've got the thing the mops are FOR.
A valve wheel, chained shut. Behind it I can hear the sea, the real one, a mile below the city.
(I open it. The water that comes knows me. It asks where it should go. I tell it: out, and then back to me.)
Subject 21. You are dripping on my floor. I run a DRY ward.
You kept me in a tank for a month.
For your own good. You leak. Drones: towels.

Hold S to GUARD her baton. Dash (L) through the orbs.
Your skills MEND you: a quarter of the damage they do comes back as health. A Tide Pool (S + U) heals you while you stand in it.
Ward Sister Purl, discharged. Against medical advice.
(Maren. Of the sea. The harbour midwives give it to a child born at the turn of the tide. I was the tide doctor. I set bones, and I drowned fevers.)
Aurelia. Med-Lab weapons annex: the Firing Gallery. A hundred paces of white corridor, and at the far end of it, a cell with a target painted on the door.
(A hundred paces. I know it is a hundred. I do not know how I know. I do not know who is doing the knowing.)
- Subject 57! Don't stand in front of the door. They test rifles on that door. I'm Wren. I live in the walls.
They brought you in because you put an arrow through a patrol drone from the next island over. They wanted to know how. Then they wanted to know if you'd still do it scared.
Sector 7's breakout emptied the gallery. The cell's on a manual latch. A and D. Press E.
The door swings. From here you can see every lamp in the corridor, and exactly how far away each one is.
Med-gel on the wall: Q to use it.
Up the scoring tower - K to jump. They hung your bow in the trophy case, unstrung. It's past the coolant spill.
Three guards, close range. Not your distance, is it? Use your elbows.
A bow of pale wood, hung on a wall like something dead. My hands string it before I have decided to.
(It hums. Not at what is near. At what is FAR. The further away I look, the surer it gets.)
Target drones, up in the rafters. They were built to be hard to hit. Hold W and show them what that means.
Subject 57. Forty years on this range and I never missed. Then you arrive and make it look easy.
It is easy. You are standing too close.
Close is where I LIKE it.

Hold S to GUARD. When he flashes white and lunges, DASH (L) through it.
Your arrows hit harder the FURTHER they fly. Vault Shot (S + U) springs you backward: make room, then shoot.
Rangemaster Keen, missed. First time for everything.
(Yara. In the harbour tongue: the far light, the one a ship steers by. They called me that because I never looked at anything close.)
Deepline. The Ice House: a meat locker the size of a station, where something very large has been kept frozen in a cage for longer than the staff have worked here.
It's dripping. Oh no. Oh no, it's DRIPPING. Mister? Mister Bear? Please don't be awake.
...Cold. I know cold. This is not my cold. Mine had a sky over it. There was a name. It is under the ice.
The Furrier bought you off a salvage crew, frozen solid in a block. Said you were the last of something. He's been waiting for the price to go up.
I'm Mitts. I stack crates. The cage latch is right there - A and D, then E. I'm not opening it. I'm just SAYING where it is.
The latch comes off in your hand. So does part of the door.
Okay. Okay okay okay. Here - pepper bun. Q when you're hurt. Please don't eat me instead.
His packers are in the next bay. He wants your hide in one piece, so they'll go easy. You, uh. Don't have to.
The madder you get the harder you hit. I've SEEN the dents in the cage. Just - point it away from me.
My centrepiece is up and walking. Packers: back in the box with it. Mind the coat.
J: attack - tap for a 4-hit combo. Your FURY grows as your health falls: the worse it gets, the harder you hit.
A block of old ice in the last cage. Inside it, a carved bear, no bigger than my thumb. A child made this.
(I break the ice. I remember the child. I remember what I did to keep the cold off her. I remember being very, very angry.)
The last of the great northern bear-men. Do you know what a pelt like yours is worth, with the head on?
More than you have.
I'll take it at cost.

Hold S to GUARD his skinning knives. His ice flasks leave freezing ground - keep moving.
When he flashes white and lunges, DASH (L) through it. The lower your health, the harder you hit: FURY.
You put the Furrier in his own freezer. I'm - I'm going to leave the door open a bit. So he doesn't keep.
(Brann. The children could not say the long name, so they said that. It means the one who stands in the door when the winter comes.)
Meat lift goes up to the Neon Market. There's an old map-maker up there. He's nice. He won't mind the, uh. Size.
The First Fold
A herder's wagon on the steppe, rain on the canvas, a child with nothing to do.
She tears a page from the tally-book and folds it. And folds it. A bird stands up in her palm and looks at her.
Her father, coming in wet, finds two of his daughter sitting on the bed, and laughs until he has to sit down, and says which one he means.
Kiri
Twice
Wolves at the lambing pen, and only one of you on watch.
So you made it two. The paper one shouted on the left while you shouted on the right.
The wolves counted, and went looking for a smaller family.
Ten Thousand Hands
The sky tore. The camp ran, and there were not enough hands to carry the children.
You folded every page of every book the clan owned. Ten thousand paper hands, each one holding somebody.
They held until the tear closed over you. Paper remembers the shape it was folded in.
Light as That
A sheet of paper does not fall. It argues with the air all the way down.
You learned to argue the same way: flat against the cliff, weighing nothing, catching every draught.
Your father said it was cheating. Your father was afraid of heights.
The Runner
The steppe, end to end, is forty days on a good horse.
A boy with a message in his shirt does it on foot in nineteen, because the horse went lame on the second day and he did not think to stop.
When he walks into the far camp they do not ask for the message. They ask who in the world he is, and he tells them.
Tarn
Uphill
A rider cut off on the ridge, raiders below.
You went up the slope at them knee-first, and did not come down again until you were on the other side of all of them.
"You could have gone ROUND," the rider said. It had not occurred to you.
Nine Hundred Miles
The sky tore, and the tear moved: east, at the pace of a walking man.
So you walked in front of it. Nine hundred miles, shouting at every camp to run, never once slower than it was.
At the edge of the steppe there was no more east. You turned round and hit it.
Straight Up
A road does not stop being a road because it has turned into a cliff.
You kept walking. Your boots found the iron in the rock, and held.
It is the same as flat ground. It is only that the horizon is behind you.
The Turn of the Tide
A frozen harbour, and under the ice the sea still breathing in and out.
A woman kneels at a hole in the ice with a sick child, and waits for the exact moment the tide turns. Then she dips him, once.
The fever goes out with the water. On the quay the mother is crying, and saying the same word over and over.
Maren
Still Water
A fishing crew carried in off the ice, frost-bitten to the knee.
You poured a ring of sea water on the infirmary floor and made them stand in it.
By morning they could feel their toes. By evening they were complaining about the smell.
The Drain
White walls. A tank. Pumps that ran all night, taking the water away.
You let them. You are patient. You were counting how much they took.
Then you asked for it back. All of it. At once. Through the walls.
Stepping on the Swell
The harbour children ran on ice they froze under their feet.
You never bothered with ice. You stepped on the water, and the water lifted you to the next step.
A tide doctor is always wanted on the far side of something.
The Far Light
The harbour mouth at night, and a ship out in the pack ice, lost, a mile off.
A girl on the sea wall lights one arrow and looses it. It comes down in the ship's dead lantern, and the lantern burns.
The pilot steers by it all the way in. On the quay he asks which of them shot, and they push her forward, and tell him.
Yara
Backwards
A white bear on the ice, too close, and coming.
You did not run. You jumped back the length of yourself and shot between its paws as you went.
It thought again. You had already nocked the second.
The Whole Sky
White walls. A hundred paces of corridor. Men with rifles who wanted to see you frightened.
You asked for your bow. They laughed, and gave it to you with one arrow.
You shot the light. In the dark, every arrow you had ever loosed came back down.
A Line to Stand On
Shoot an arrow with a cord on it into the far side of anything.
Then walk the cord. The harbour children freeze their steps. You string yours.
It only has to hold for as long as you are looking at the other end.
The One in the Door
A long-house on the high steppe, snowed in to the eaves, and something scratching at the door.
A very large man gets up from the fire, opens it, and stands in the gap. All night. In the morning there are tracks, and they stop a pace from his feet.
The children cannot manage his whole name. They make it shorter, and shout it when they are frightened.
Brann
Loud
Raiders at the winter stores, forty of them.
You did not fight them. You stood up on the roof-beam and told them, at the top of your voice, what you were.
The horses left first. The riders had no choice in the matter.
Rolling Down
The sky tore above the high pasture, and the herd bolted for the cliff.
You went down the mountain faster than the herd. You do not remember your feet touching it.
You were at the bottom when they arrived. You were in the way. That was the point.
Claws
Bears climb. People forget that.
You learned from the old sow on the ridge, who went up a rock face after honey as if it were a staircase.
She let you watch. Once. Then she chased you up it.
There are two of you in my doorway, and one of you is rustling. Sit down, both. Look at the tags: the storm-eye. The old mark of Vharra.
You walked here. From Mile Zero. Without once asking the way. Sit, lad, before you wear a groove in my floor. Look at the tags: the storm-eye. The mark of Vharra.
Mind the lintel. And the shelves. And - never mind, I can draw another. Look at the tags, big one: the storm-eye. The old mark of Vharra.
A wagon in the rain. A paper bird standing in my hand. I saw it in the shard.
The steppe, end to end, on foot. A camp asking who I was. I saw it in the shard.
A long-house under snow. Children shouting a short name. I saw it in the shard.
A folder. The paper-clans kept our tally and our stories; I thought every page of them burned. The tear shredded what we WERE, girl - memory, power - into Memory Shards.
A runner of the far camps. You carried word faster than horses. The tear shredded what we WERE, lad - memory, power - into Memory Shards.
One of the door-wardens of the high steppe. There were never many. The tear shredded what we WERE - memory, power - into Memory Shards.
